title: Christian Ethics
description: How Christians discern and do what is good. Students study the foundations of Christian ethics (Scripture, natural law, virtue, the Ten Commandments, love), major ethical methods (divine command, natural law, virtue, situational and consequentialist alternatives), and apply them to life and death, sexuality and marriage, wealth and work, truth-telling, war and peace, justice and race, the state, technology and creation care. Where faithful Christians disagree (e.g. just war and pacifism) the major views are presented from their sources.

quiz_bank.question: State the strongest case for Christian pacifism.
quiz_bank.answer_key: Jesus' teaching to love enemies and not resist evil (Matt 5), his own nonviolence and the cross, the early church's widespread refusal of military service, the church as a distinct kingdom people, and the eschatological vision of peace (Isa 2) - as held by Anabaptists and others.
